question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

By the time I turn thirty / I would had visited every / continent in the world and have gained / a wealth of knowledge and experience.
option_1: By the time I turn thirty
option_2: a wealth of knowledge and experience
option_4: continent in the world and have gained
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I would had visited every.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence talks about an action that will be completed before a point of time in the future ("By the time I turn thirty"). Such a situation needs the Future Perfect Tense, whose structure is "will have + V3 (past participle)".

• The segment "I would had visited" is doubly wrong:

◦ After the modal "would", only the base form (V1) can follow — never "had". So "would had" is impossible in English.

◦ The correct future-perfect form here is "I would have visited" / "I will have visited".

• The rest of the sentence ("and have gained") is coordinated with "have visited", so the intended structure is "I would have visited ... and have gained".

◦ Correct: By the time I turn thirty, I would have visited every continent in the world and have gained a wealth of knowledge and experience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "By the time I turn thirty" is correct — with a "by the time" clause referring to the future, the simple present ("I turn") is used, not "will turn".

• Option 4 "continent in the world and have gained" is correct — "every + singular noun" (every continent) and the parallel perfect form "have gained".

• Option 2 "a wealth of knowledge and experience" is a correct noun phrase; "a wealth of" means a large amount of.

NOTE

• Modal + V1 always: would go, could see, should write, must be. Modal + have + V3 for the perfect: would have gone, should have written.

• Future Perfect: Subject + will/shall have + V3 + by/by the time ... — "She will have finished the report by Monday."

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is a / (B) state of chaos / (C) since the / (D) chairman resigned.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a sentence contains "since + a point of time / a past event", the main clause must be in the Present Perfect or Present Perfect Continuous, not in the Simple Present.

• Part (A) "It is a" uses the simple present. It should be "It has been a" — the state of chaos began when the chairman resigned and continues up to now.

◦ Correct: It has been a state of chaos since the chairman resigned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Part (B) "state of chaos" is a correct noun phrase (chaos = complete disorder / अव्यवस्था).

• Part (C) "since the" correctly introduces the time clause.

• Part (D) "chairman resigned" is correct — the clause after "since" takes the simple past.

NOTE

• Rule: Present Perfect + since + Simple Past. "I have known him since we were children." / "She has been ill since Monday."

• Use "since" with a point of time (since 2019, since Monday) and "for" with a period of time (for three years).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

The apple of one’s eye
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Very dear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the apple of one's eye" means a person (or thing) that is cherished above all others; someone very dear and precious. (आँखों का तारा)

◦ Example: His youngest daughter is the apple of his eye.

• The expression is very old (it appears in the Bible and in Old English) — the "apple" originally meant the pupil of the eye, the most precious and protected part of the body.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Very cheerful", Option 3 "Very nice" and Option 4 "Very pleasing" describe a mood or a quality; the idiom expresses affection and preciousness, not cheerfulness or pleasantness.

• The idiom is always used for a person or thing that is loved deeply, usually by a parent, grandparent or teacher.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of affection: "near and dear", "close to one's heart", "the light of one's life", "one's better half" (spouse).

• Other "apple" idioms: "apple of discord" (a cause of quarrel), "upset the apple cart" (to spoil a plan), "a bad apple" (a person who spoils a group).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Harmony
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Conflict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harmony" means agreement, peaceful co-existence and accord among people; in music it means a pleasing combination of notes. (सामंजस्य / मेल-जोल)

• Its antonym is "Conflict", which means a serious disagreement, clash or quarrel. (संघर्ष / टकराव)

◦ Example: The two communities lived in harmony for years until a conflict broke out over land.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Unity" (oneness, togetherness) is a synonym of harmony, not its antonym.

• Option 1 "Adaptability" (the ability to adjust to new conditions) and Option 2 "Clarity" (clearness) are unrelated to the idea of agreement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of harmony: accord, concord, unity, agreement, rapport, consonance.

• Antonyms of harmony: conflict, discord, disagreement, strife, friction, dissonance.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Pandemics have often been caused by a disease that spreads by physical touch or contact.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. are contagious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Contagious" means (of a disease) spread from one person to another by direct or indirect physical contact. It is therefore the exact one-word replacement for "spreads by physical touch or contact". (संक्रामक)

◦ Correct: Pandemics have often been caused by diseases that are contagious.

• Diseases such as influenza, COVID-19, chickenpox and the common cold are contagious because touching an infected person or a surface they have touched can transmit them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "vigorous" means energetic, forceful and strong — it describes effort or health, not the manner in which a disease spreads.

• Option 3 "robust" means sturdy and strong (a robust economy, a robust body) — again, not about transmission.

• Option 4 "fastidious" means very attentive to detail; hard to please; fussy about cleanliness — completely unrelated to disease transmission.

NOTE

• Distinguish: contagious (spread by touch/contact) vs infectious (spread by air, water, food or germs generally) vs communicable (any disease that can be passed on).

• Related words: contagion (the spreading of disease by contact), epidemic (an outbreak in one region), pandemic (an outbreak across countries/continents), endemic (regularly found in a particular area).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

The two neighbours will probably stop fighting when pigs fly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Something that is impossible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "when pigs fly" is used to say that something will never happen because it is impossible. Since pigs obviously cannot fly, the phrase expresses total disbelief. (असंभव बात / जब कभी नहीं)

◦ Example: "He will apologise when pigs fly." (= He will never apologise.)

• In the sentence, it means the two quarrelsome neighbours are never going to stop fighting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "When their families meet" and Option 4 "When it rains" wrongly treat the idiom literally, as if it named a real occasion.

• Option 2 "When there is magic" is close to the idea of the unbelievable, but the idiom specifically stresses impossibility, not magic.

NOTE

• Similar idioms meaning "never": "when hell freezes over", "once in a blue moon" (extremely rarely), "not in a million years", "till the cows come home" (for a very long time).

• Remember: idioms must be interpreted figuratively, never word by word.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her dedication to her work was _______ what anyone had expected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. beyond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beyond" here means more than / surpassing / exceeding a limit. "Beyond what anyone had expected" = far greater than anybody's expectation. (अपेक्षा से कहीं अधिक)

◦ Correct: Her dedication to her work was beyond what anyone had expected.

• "Beyond + expectation/imagination/doubt/repair/control" is a very common collocation pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "over" indicates position above something or an amount ("over fifty people"); it is not used before a noun clause such as "what anyone had expected".

• Option 3 "beside" means "next to / at the side of" (Sit beside me). Do not confuse it with "besides" (in addition to).

• Option 4 "through" means from one end to the other; by means of — it does not convey exceeding expectations.

NOTE

• Useful "beyond" phrases: beyond doubt (certain), beyond repair (cannot be mended), beyond one's means (too costly), beyond belief (unbelievable), beyond the pale (unacceptable).

question:
There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

He was in despare because of the expiry of his licence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. despare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Despare" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "despair", meaning complete loss of hope. (निराशा / हताशा)

◦ Correct: He was in despair because of the expiry of his licence.

• Spelling key: DE + SPAIR (it ends in -air, like "air", not "-are").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Expiry" (the end of the period of validity) is correctly spelt.

• "Because" is correctly spelt (BE + CAUSE).

• "Licence" is correctly spelt in British English as a noun; the American spelling is "license". (In British usage, "licence" = noun, "license" = verb.)

NOTE

• Word family: despair (noun/verb), desperate (adjective — hopeless, reckless), desperation (noun), despairingly (adverb).

• Commonly confused pairs: practice (noun)/practise (verb), advice (noun)/advise (verb), licence (noun)/license (verb) in British English.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Demolish
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Construct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Demolish" means to pull down, destroy or completely tear apart a building or structure. (ध्वस्त करना / गिरा देना)

• Its antonym is "Construct", meaning to build or put together. (निर्माण करना)

◦ Example: The corporation will demolish the old market and construct a new complex there.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Invite" (to ask someone to come) and Option 4 "Appreciate" (to value or admire) are unrelated to building or destroying.

• Option 2 "Criticise" (to find fault with) is not the opposite of demolish in the physical sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of demolish: destroy, raze, flatten, wreck, dismantle, tear down.

• Antonyms of demolish: construct, build, erect, raise, assemble, establish.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. junior than all.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Adjectives of Latin origin ending in "-or" — junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior, posterior, anterior — are followed by the preposition "to", never by "than".

• Therefore "junior than all his colleagues" is wrong; it must be "junior to all his colleagues".

◦ Correct: Tushar is junior to all his colleagues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "is" is the correct singular verb for the singular subject "Tushar".

• Option 3 "Tushar" (proper noun) and Option 4 "his colleagues" are both correct.

• Note also that these Latin comparatives never take "more/most": "more superior" and "most senior than" are wrong.

NOTE

• Latin comparatives + to: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, prior to, preferable to, elder to (in Indian usage).

• Example sentences: "This model is superior to that one." / "He joined prior to the merger." / "Tea is preferable to coffee for me."

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Enchanted
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Appealing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enchanted" means charmed, delighted, filled with great pleasure; bewitched by something attractive. (मंत्रमुग्ध / मोहित)

• Among the given options, "Appealing" — meaning attractive, charming, pleasing — is the closest in sense, because whatever enchants is by definition appealing.

◦ Example: The children were enchanted by the appealing beauty of the valley.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Disgusted" (filled with strong distaste) is an antonym.

• Option 4 "Repelling" (driving away; causing dislike) is also an antonym.

• Option 2 "Cursed" (under an evil spell) suggests something harmful — enchanted is a positive word here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enchanted: charmed, captivated, enthralled, spellbound, fascinated, delighted, bewitched.

• Antonyms of enchanted: disgusted, repelled, bored, repulsed, disenchanted.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

By the skin of your teeth
option_2: To be less affected by criticisms and rebuffs
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. By a very narrow margin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "by the skin of one's teeth" means just barely; by a very narrow margin; only just managing to succeed or escape. (बाल-बाल बचना / बहुत कम अंतर से)

◦ Example: He caught the last train by the skin of his teeth.

◦ Example: She passed the examination by the skin of her teeth.

• The phrase comes from the Book of Job in the Bible; since teeth have no skin, the margin referred to is vanishingly thin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To be less affected by criticisms and rebuffs" is the meaning of a different idiom — "to have a thick skin".

• Option 3 "Very protective" is unrelated.

• Option 4 "Saved by others" is wrong — the idiom describes a narrow escape, not who did the saving.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "a close shave", "a narrow escape", "touch and go", "by a hair's breadth", "in the nick of time".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) One of / (B) my brothers write / (C) novels for / (D) leisure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the structure "One of + plural noun + singular verb", the subject of the sentence is "One" (singular), not the plural noun that follows "of". Hence the verb must be singular.

• Part (B) has "my brothers write" (plural verb). It should be "my brothers writes".

◦ Correct: One of my brothers writes novels for leisure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "One of" is correct, and it must be followed by a plural noun ("brothers"), which it is.

• Part (C) "novels for" and Part (D) "leisure" are correct — "for leisure" means for pleasure/relaxation.

NOTE

• Rule: One of + plural noun + singular verb — "One of the boys is absent." / "One of my friends lives in Delhi."

• But in a relative clause the verb follows the plural noun: "He is one of the boys who are absent." (Here "who" refers to "boys".)

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. and good communicator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two different roles, qualities or persons are mentioned, the article must be repeated before each noun. Here "an excellent writer" and "a good communicator" are two distinct capacities, so the second noun also needs its own article.

• The segment should be "and a good communicator".

◦ Correct: Henry is known as an excellent writer and a good communicator in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Henry is known" is correct (passive form of "know").

• Option 1 "as an excellent writer" is correct — "as" is used to state the capacity in which someone is known, and "an" is correct before the vowel sound of "excellent".

• Option 2 "in English" is correct.

NOTE

• Article rule: repeat the article for two separate people/things — "He met a poet and a novelist" (two persons); omit it if one person holds both roles — "He met a poet and novelist" (one person who is both).

• Use "a" before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin) and "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an M.A. degree).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Chronology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chronology" is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence. (कालक्रम / घटनाक्रम)

◦ Example: The historian prepared a chronology of the freedom struggle.

• Root: Greek "chronos" = time + "logia" = study. Hence "chronological order" = time order.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Theology" = the study of religion and God. (धर्मशास्त्र)

• Option 3 "Entomology" = the study of insects. (कीट विज्ञान)

• Option 4 "Psychology" = the study of the mind and behaviour. (मनोविज्ञान)

NOTE

• More "-logy" words for SSC: etymology (origin of words), ornithology (birds), anthropology (human beings and societies), archaeology (ancient remains), geology (the earth), pathology (diseases), cardiology (the heart), seismology (earthquakes).

question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

As soon as Rohan learned that he had topped the examination, he was on cloud nine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very happy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on cloud nine" means extremely happy, delighted or elated. (अत्यंत प्रसन्न / फूला न समाना)

◦ Example: She was on cloud nine when she got the government job.

• The context — Rohan learning that he had topped the examination — clearly signals great joy, so "very happy" is the meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Very tense" and Option 4 "Very confused" express anxiety, the opposite of the joy suggested here.

• Option 2 "Very sad" is a direct antonym of the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of happiness: "over the moon", "on top of the world", "in seventh heaven", "walking on air", "jump for joy".

• Idioms of sadness: "down in the dumps", "feeling blue", "a long face", "heart of lead".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His research on the migratory patterns of the birds is run-of-the-mill.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. average.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Run-of-the-mill" means ordinary, commonplace, not special in any way — just average. (साधारण / मामूली)

◦ Example: It was a run-of-the-mill film with nothing new to offer.

• The phrase comes from the milling industry: goods that came straight off the mill, before being sorted for quality, were of ordinary, unremarkable standard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "absurd" means ridiculous or illogical — a much stronger, negative judgement than "ordinary".

• Option 2 "one in a million" means exceptionally rare and special — the exact opposite of run-of-the-mill.

• Option 3 "trash" means worthless rubbish — again far more negative than "average".

NOTE

• Synonyms of run-of-the-mill: average, ordinary, mediocre, unremarkable, commonplace, everyday, garden-variety.

• Antonyms: exceptional, outstanding, extraordinary, remarkable, one in a million.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The politician guaranted that he would create jobs if elected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. guaranteed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "guaranted" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "guaranteed", the past form of the verb "guarantee", meaning to promise firmly that something will be done or will happen. (गारंटी देना / वचन देना)

◦ Correct: The politician guaranteed that he would create jobs if elected.

• Spelling key: G-U-A-R-A-N-T-E-E-D — note the "ua" after G, a single "r", and the double "ee" before "d".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gurranted" — wrong: the "ua" is missing and the "r" is doubled.

• Option 2 "gauaranteed" — wrong: an extra "a" after "g".

• Option 3 "guarranteed" — wrong: the "r" is wrongly doubled.

NOTE

• Word family: guarantee (verb/noun), guaranteed (past/past participle), guarantor (a person who gives a guarantee), warranty (a written guarantee for a product).

• Other tricky "gu-" spellings: guard, guardian, guess, guest, guide, guilty, guitar.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The old man distributed his property ________ his ten grandchildren equally.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. among.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Among" is used when something is shared or distributed between more than two persons or things. Here the property is divided among ten grandchildren.

◦ Correct: The old man distributed his property among his ten grandchildren equally.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "between" is used for two persons/things (or for clearly separate individual items) — "Divide the sweets between the two boys."

• Option 1 "within" means inside the limits of (within the campus, within an hour) — it cannot show distribution.

• Option 3 "towards" shows direction or attitude (walking towards the gate, kindness towards animals), not distribution.

NOTE

• Rule: between = two; among/amongst = more than two.

• Related preposition pairs for SSC: in/into, on/upon, beside/besides, since/for, by/until, in/within.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Indispensible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indispensible" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "indispensable", meaning absolutely necessary; that cannot be done without. (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

◦ Example: Water is indispensable for life.

• Spelling key: IN + DISPENS + ABLE (it takes "-able", not "-ible").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Paraphernalia" (miscellaneous articles or equipment associated with an activity) is correctly spelt.

• "Handkerchiefs" (the plural of handkerchief) is correctly spelt — nouns ending in "-f/-fe" preceded by "ie" here simply add "-s".

• "Conjuror" (a magician; also spelt "conjurer") is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Common "-able" words: indispensable, inevitable, comfortable, admirable, dependable, memorable.

• Common "-ible" words: possible, sensible, terrible, visible, responsible, incredible, permissible.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Medical hand practices have been an integral part of healthcare for centuries, but with technological advancements, machines are (1)________ taking over. Robotic surgeries, for instance, have become increasingly popular, allowing surgeons to perform complex (2)________ with minimal invasive techniques. Machine learning and artificial intelligence have transformed medical diagnosis by analysing large amounts of patient data and providing highly detailed medical images. However, there are still challenges to overcome in the use of these technologies in healthcare. For example, the cost of purchasing and maintaining medical machines can be high, and there are concerns around the ethical use of AI in medicine. Nonetheless, it is clear that medical hand practices are (3)________ to machines, and these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry. Additionally, the use of telemedicine and remote monitoring devices allows patients to receive medical care from the (4)________ of their homes, particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas. Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. gradually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gradually" means slowly, step by step, over a period of time. (धीरे-धीरे)

• The passage describes a long-term, ongoing shift — machines have been advancing "for centuries" and are steadily replacing manual medical practice. Hence "machines are gradually taking over" is the natural adverb.

◦ Correct: ... with technological advancements, machines are gradually taking over.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sincerely" (honestly, genuinely) describes a person's attitude and cannot describe a technological process.

• Option 2 "partially" (in part, not completely) contradicts the sentence's idea of machines "taking over".

• Option 4 "deliberately" (intentionally, on purpose) implies conscious intention, which machines do not have.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner/degree frequently tested: gradually, steadily, rapidly, entirely, partially, deliberately, inadvertently.

• Fill-in-the-blank strategy: read the whole passage first, identify the tone (here, an account of steady change), and check which word fits both grammar and meaning.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Medical hand practices have been an integral part of healthcare for centuries, but with technological advancements, machines are (1)________ taking over. Robotic surgeries, for instance, have become increasingly popular, allowing surgeons to perform complex (2)________ with minimal invasive techniques. Machine learning and artificial intelligence have transformed medical diagnosis by analysing large amounts of patient data and providing highly detailed medical images. However, there are still challenges to overcome in the use of these technologies in healthcare. For example, the cost of purchasing and maintaining medical machines can be high, and there are concerns around the ethical use of AI in medicine. Nonetheless, it is clear that medical hand practices are (3)________ to machines, and these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry. Additionally, the use of telemedicine and remote monitoring devices allows patients to receive medical care from the (4)________ of their homes, particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas. Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. procedures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "procedure" in medicine means a surgical or medical operation carried out on a patient. The sentence speaks of robotic surgeries that allow surgeons to "perform complex procedures with minimal invasive techniques". (शल्य प्रक्रियाएँ)

• The collocation "perform a procedure" is the standard medical expression, and the plural "procedures" agrees with the plural adjective phrase "complex".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "therapies" refers to treatment courses (physiotherapy, chemotherapy) — these are not what surgeons "perform" in a surgery.

• Option 2 "diagnosis" is the identification of a disease; it is also singular, so "complex diagnosis" does not match, and diagnosis is discussed separately later in the passage.

• Option 3 "analysis" (singular; plural = analyses) refers to detailed examination of data, not to surgery.

NOTE

• Collocations: perform an operation/a procedure/surgery; make a diagnosis; carry out an analysis; undergo treatment.

• Note the plurals: diagnosis → diagnoses, analysis → analyses, crisis → crises, thesis → theses.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. evolving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evolving" means developing or changing gradually into something else. (विकसित होना / क्रमिक रूप से बदलना)

• The whole passage is about progress and transformation — manual medical practice is not merely shrinking, it is changing into machine-based practice. The very next clause says "these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry", which confirms a positive idea of development.

◦ Correct: ... it is clear that medical hand practices are evolving to machines ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "diminishing" (becoming smaller) and Option 3 "depleting" (using up a resource until it runs short) both express mere reduction, and neither takes "to machines" naturally.

• Option 4 "stagnating" (remaining still, showing no growth) directly contradicts the passage's theme of rapid advancement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of evolve: develop, progress, advance, transform, unfold. Antonyms: stagnate, regress, decline.

• Note the related noun evolution and the adjective evolutionary.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Medical hand practices have been an integral part of healthcare for centuries, but with technological advancements, machines are (1)________ taking over. Robotic surgeries, for instance, have become increasingly popular, allowing surgeons to perform complex (2)________ with minimal invasive techniques. Machine learning and artificial intelligence have transformed medical diagnosis by analysing large amounts of patient data and providing highly detailed medical images. However, there are still challenges to overcome in the use of these technologies in healthcare. For example, the cost of purchasing and maintaining medical machines can be high, and there are concerns around the ethical use of AI in medicine. Nonetheless, it is clear that medical hand practices are (3)________ to machines, and these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry. Additionally, the use of telemedicine and remote monitoring devices allows patients to receive medical care from the (4)________ of their homes, particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas. Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. comfort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "from the comfort of one's home" means without having to leave home; in an easy, relaxed way. (घर बैठे आराम से)

• Telemedicine and remote monitoring devices let patients receive care without travelling — this is exactly the idea of "from the comfort of their homes", which is why it is "particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "locality" means a neighbourhood or area; "from the locality of their homes" is not idiomatic English.

• Option 3 "range" means the distance or extent something covers — it does not fit "from the ... of their homes".

• Option 4 "inconvenience" (trouble, difficulty) reverses the meaning; the whole point is that telemedicine removes inconvenience.

NOTE

• Common collocations with comfort: in the comfort of, comfort zone, creature comforts, words of comfort.

• Word family: comfort (noun/verb), comfortable (adjective), comfortably (adverb), discomfort (antonym noun).

Robotic surgeries, for instance, have become increasingly popular, allowing surgeons to perform complex (2)________ with minimal invasive techniques. Machine learning and artificial intelligence have transformed medical diagnosis by analysing large amounts of patient data and providing highly detailed medical images. However, there are still challenges to overcome in the use of these technologies in healthcare. For example, the cost of purchasing and maintaining medical machines can be high, and there are concerns around the ethical use of AI in medicine. Nonetheless, it is clear that medical hand practices are (3)________ to machines, and these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry. Additionally, the use of telemedicine and remote monitoring devices allows patients to receive medical care from the (4)________ of their homes, particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas. Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. enabling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enable" means to make someone able to do something; to give them the means or opportunity. It takes the structure "enable + object + to + verb", which exactly matches "enabling them to make informed decisions".

◦ Correct: ... machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, enabling them to make informed decisions ...

• Real-time information is what makes it possible for doctors to decide quickly and adjust treatment plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "reimagining" (thinking about something in a new way) does not take "them to make ..." and does not fit the cause-effect link.

• Option 2 "adapting" means adjusting to new conditions; "adapting them to make decisions" changes the meaning entirely.

• Option 3 "neglecting" (ignoring, failing to care for) is negative and contradicts the benefit being described.

NOTE

• Verbs taking "object + to-infinitive": enable, allow, permit, encourage, force, persuade, advise, request, remind, warn.

• The "-ing" form here is a participle phrase showing the result of the main clause — "The bridge collapsed, blocking the road."
